title: Over- and under-treatment of hypothyroidism is associated with excess mortality: a register-based cohort study
authors: Lillevang-Johansen M, Abrahamsen B, Jørgensen HL, Brix TH, Hegedüs L
population: Danish individuals with at least one TSH measurement in 1995 to 2011; hypothyroidism defined by two TSH values above 4.0 mIU/l or one such value with two levothyroxine prescriptions
funder: Funding statement not read: the publisher's full text returned HTTP 403 to automated access, and no open copy was found.
result: Mortality was increased in untreated hypothyroid individuals (n = 673; HR 1.46, 95% CI 1.26 to 1.69) against euthyroid controls. Each 6 months with raised TSH increased mortality in treated and untreated individuals (HR 1.05, 1.02 to 1.07, for each). In levothyroxine-treated patients each 6 months with decreased TSH increased mortality by a factor of 1.18 (1.15 to 1.21), essentially unchanged by severity of hypothyroidism and by age below or above 65 years. Results read from the PubMed abstract.
